_note: The race commentary (GDD 4.3.1, step R4). Texts only: scripts/core/race_commentary.gd turns the race's events (Race.events), the player's choices (Race.say_log, Race.card_log) and the race state into lines. A line is a string or {t, when}. `when` is a set of conditions on the event's context: key: value (equal), key: [a, b] (one of), key: true / false, key_min / key_max (number at least / at most). Keys: shape (fast / honest / tactical), tier, style (yle / mtv), indoor, kind (race / sections / heat / semi / final), chase, player (the event is about the player), involves_player (the other runner is the player), known (the personality of the runner is known to the player: met twice), personality (front / pack / kicker / surger), mark, pos, leader, to_go, d, gap, vs_even, group, spread, way, where, seconds, lost, margin, place, pb, sb, late (to_go 200 or less), lap (1 / 2). Placeholders: {name} the runner's surname, {full}, {first}, {club}, {other} a second runner's surname, {to_go}, {m} metres run, {pos} place (3rd), {gap} metres behind the leader, {mark}, {split} (time at the mark), {vs} (percent faster / slower than the field's even pace), {group}, {spread}, {leader}, {time}, {margin}, {bell} (The bell / Halfway) and {bell_l}, {pname} the player's surname, {field}, {meet}, {round}, {coach_name}, plus the facts of fillers. A line is used at most once per race and the last `rules.memory` lines used are avoided across races. Voices: tv (the commentator, selostaja), expert (asiantuntija, a former athlete or coach: analysis, background), announcer (the stadium announcer of a small meet), you (the player's own choices), fan (another runner's supporter), coach (data/coaches.json). All names are made up. Style yle = sober and factual, mtv = colourful with more history. Who talks: tiers (by the meet's level, level_tier): announcer = the stadium announcer alone (local and district meets), stream = one commentator, no expert (national championships such as Nuorten SM, streamed; decision 47), stream_expert = commentator + expert (international youth meets streamed), tv = commentator + expert (senior championships, TV). More keys: grouped (the race is a heat / semi-final / section: its winner 'wins the heat', its places are no medals, decision 43), medal (the place in the event is a real medal place: a single race, a final, or the overall place of the last section), scope and the placeholders {in_part} (' in the heat' for a heat or section place, else empty), {win_obj} ('it' / 'the heat' / 'the section') and {win_of} (the same as ' of the heat'), fav_club (the favourite has a club). Talk between the calls (`fillers`) only on lap 1 and 1-2 facts (decision 45); introductions, the season, the next meet and history are parked in `ceremony`. The crew knows the style of the `rules.crew_favourites` best-marked rivals at streamed and TV meets (decision 46). `verdicts` are the 10 s 'so far' lines (neutral on moves: `move_neutral`), `verdicts_final` the real verdict on each choice, told in the Race story (decision 44).

ceremony.t: Finland has a long distance-running tradition, going back to the days of Paavo Nurmi. The 800 has had fewer headlines, but plenty of quality.
ceremony.reply: The best runners here come from small clubs and long winters. That says something about the sport.

ceremony.t: {pfull}, {page} years old, running for {pclub}. This is how careers begin.
In the stands by the 200 metre start, {coach_name}, the coach of {pname}, is watching every stride.
ceremony.reply: A coach in the stands sees things the athlete doesn't. The shouts carry further than you'd think.

ceremony.t: At the rail of the hall, {coach_name}, the coach of {pname}, follows every lap.
ceremony.reply: Indoors the coach can see the whole track, so every lap gets a comment.

ceremony.t: Welcome to {meet}. The 800 metres is under way.

story._rules: Playtest fix 5 (2026-10-10): a kick that began with late_kick_to_go m or less to go and still died is kick_died_late (the pace before it was the problem), not 'too early'; a time more than better_pct % faster than the athlete's own best (season best, else PB) is 'better'; 'below' needs a time more than below_pct % slower than it too; a PB (against an earlier mark) is its own case 'pb'; a season best stands in for as_expected / below ('sb').
